question: Who will win the 2026 Georgia governor's race — Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms or Republican Rick Jackson — in the open seat left by term-limited Brian Kemp?
title: Georgia Governor — Bottoms vs. Jackson
resolution: Resolves to the winner of the Georgia governor general election on Nov 3, 2026 — or a December runoff if no candidate clears 50%.

consensus.headline_case: Bottoms is favored, but this is a lean, not a lock. Three real-money and regulated markets — Polymarket, Kalshi, PredictIt — converge in the mid-50s for the Democrat, and that convergence firmed after Republican Rick Jackson declined Bottoms's June debate challenge, a real dated event that moved PredictIt from 46% to 54% and Kalshi into the mid-to-high 50s. Georgia's underlying environment helps her: Trump's net approval in the state is underwater by 8-10 points, and 2018 (the last time an R president faced a first midterm) saw Democrats flip seven Republican-held governorships. But Jackson has poured over $100 million of his own money into the race and hasn't spent most of it yet, a June Wick Research poll had the race dead even, and Georgia's own gubernatorial history swings wildly (Kemp won by 1.4 points in 2018, then 7.5 in 2022) rather than settling into a predictable band. Landing the consensus in the low-to-mid 50s, not the high 50s the raw market composite implies, respects both the real signal and the real uncertainty.
consensus.why_over_runner_up: Jackson's path is live and underpriced by more than the market composite alone suggests, because $87 million of his ad blitz is only now hitting airwaves and a single near-tied poll (Wick, June 27-30) shows the race is not settled. But he stays the runner-up: he has never won a general election as a candidate, he beat Trump's own endorsed pick (Burt Jones) in the primary in a way that risks depressing MAGA-base turnout in November, and he is on the wrong side of a national environment where the president's party is historically likely to lose ground. His refusal to debate, while it could still be reversed, currently reads to markets as a tell, not a strategy.
consensus.dissent: The Contrarian's case doesn't die easily: a $60,000-volume Polymarket book and a Kalshi/PredictIt pair moved by one campaign-scheduling story are thin foundations for a mid-50s call three months out. Kemp leaves office with roughly 60% approval and a +33 net favorability rating — Georgians like Republican governance even while they sour on Trump nationally, and that split-ticket habit (Kemp romped in 2022 the same cycle Herschel Walker lost the Senate seat) is exactly the pattern Jackson needs. If the Wick poll's near-tie is closer to the true electorate than the market-moving debate story, Jackson belongs in the high-40s, not the low-40s.

profiles.name: The Market Reader
profiles.criterion: Sides with the price the sharpest, deepest, most liquid markets have settled on.
profiles.blurb: Three separate books, three separate mechanisms, one direction. Polymarket prints Bottoms at 59% on $59,978 traded since an October 2025 launch. Kalshi's GOVPARTYGA-26 has run 55-58% Democrat depending on the pull date. PredictIt has her at 54%. None of these are the Kalshi-Senate-grade liquidity I'd like - Polymarket's book is thin - but three independent venues landing within five points of each other after the same debate-dodge news is a real signal, not noise. I take the composite and don't fight it, I just don't round it up to the high end.
profiles.evidence: Polymarket 59% ($59,978 vol, launched Oct 13 2025); Kalshi GOVPARTYGA-26 55-58%; PredictIt 54%; pulled late Jul-early Aug 2026.

profiles.name: The Quant
profiles.criterion: Trusts the simulation models and structured decompositions over recency and sentiment.
profiles.blurb: Take the odds, not the probabilities, from each market and geometric-mean them: Polymarket 59/41, Kalshi (midpoint) 56.5/43.5, PredictIt 54/46. That product-root comes out to roughly 0.567 for Bottoms. Now discount it: Polymarket's $60k book is thin enough to overweight in a naive average, and the Wick poll's near-tie is real information the markets may be lagging. Shave two to three points off the raw composite for those two frictions and the number that survives is 55%, not 57-59%.
profiles.evidence: Geometric mean of Polymarket/Kalshi/PredictIt odds ~ 0.567, discounted ~2-3pts for thin Polymarket volume and the unresolved Wick-poll near-tie.

profiles.name: The Historian
profiles.criterion: Counted reference-class base rates and venue history.
profiles.blurb: I count what this state has actually done and it refuses to give me a clean rhythm. Kemp beat Abrams by 1.4 points in 2018, then by 7.5 in 2022 - no steady drumbeat there, just wide variance I cannot pretend into a tight band. So I turn to the wider ledger: in 2018, the last first midterm of a Republican president, Democrats took seven Republican-held governor's mansions, and Trump's own net approval sits eight to ten points underwater in Georgia today. The venue's own history offers no comfort to either side; the out-party ledger tips me, gently, toward Bottoms.
profiles.evidence: GA governor margins: 1.4pts (2018), 7.5pts (2022) - wide variance, no tight streak; 7 GOP-held governorships flipped D in 2018's first-midterm wave; Trump GA net approval -8 to -10 (Apr/Jun 2026 polls).

profiles.name: The Path Reader
profiles.criterion: Ignores reputation; reads the actual route, mechanism, and path dependence.
profiles.blurb: Follow what actually happened, not what either side says. Bottoms challenged Jackson to debate on June 23. He never answered. That's not a campaign being cautious - that's a campaign whose internal numbers told it a stage next to a first-time, self-funded candidate is a bad trade, and the market moved eight points on exactly that read. Jackson still has $87 million of ad spend not yet fully deployed, which is the live counter-mechanism. But a candidate who won't debate three months out is running from something. Narrow Bottoms.
profiles.evidence: Bottoms's June 23 debate challenge went unanswered; Kalshi/PredictIt moved Bottoms from ~46% to 54-55% between late June and mid-July on that news; Jackson's $87M ad blitz still mostly unspent as of the pull date.

profiles.name: The Talisman
profiles.criterion: Elite individual actors, motivation, proven leadership.
profiles.blurb: I read the man, not the tape. Here is someone raised in foster care who built a healthcare-staffing empire, then walked into a primary against a sitting lieutenant governor carrying Donald Trump's own endorsement - and beat him, spending over $108 million of his own fortune to do it. That is not a candidate who folds. A debate declined is not always fear; sometimes it is a disciplined operation that refuses to hand its opponent oxygen. I back the man who has already out-executed the state party machine once this cycle to do it again.
profiles.evidence: Jackson: foster-care background, self-made Jackson Healthcare founder; beat Trump-endorsed Burt Jones in the June 16 runoff; $108M+ self-funded, incl. an $87M ad blitz.

profiles.name: The Contrarian
profiles.criterion: Favorites usually fail; hunts the underpriced live path.
profiles.blurb: Everybody's leaning on a market that moved eight points because a candidate skipped one debate invitation in June. That's thin gruel to hang a mid-50s call on, especially with Polymarket's book barely bigger than a poker night's buy-in. Meanwhile Kemp leaves office at roughly 60% approval and a +33 net - Georgians clearly distinguish 'Republican governor' from 'Trump fatigue,' the same split-ticket habit that let Kemp cruise in 2022 the same cycle Walker lost the Senate seat. And the one poll actually taken after the runoff, Wick's, had this dead even. I'll take Jackson in the mid-40s and let the fall polling catch up.
profiles.evidence: Polymarket volume only ~$59,978; Wick poll (Jun 27-30) had Jackson 43.2 / Bottoms 42.7; Kemp GA approval ~60%, net +33, exiting as a Republican governor.

profiles.name: The Prophet
profiles.criterion: Divine providence; backs the fated, story-shaped outcome the ending events seem to be scripting.
profiles.blurb: Look at the shape of the story being written. A mayor who once governed the state's capital through its hardest recent years steps back onto the stage, and the party that nominates her turns out more voters in the primary than the other side does for the first time in two decades. That is not incidental; that is a base finding its footing again. The man across from her built an empire and a fortune, but fortune bought him the nomination, not the mandate - the crowd that shows up in May is telling you who it thinks belongs in November.
profiles.evidence: Bottoms, former Atlanta mayor, nominated after Democratic 2026 primary turnout exceeded Republican turnout for the first time since 2006.

base_rates.text: Geometric-mean composite across the three exact-question markets with real trading (Polymarket 59%, Kalshi 55-58%, PredictIt 54%), pulled late July-early Aug 2026 - the strongest available anchor, though thinner than a typical federal-race market.

Georgia gubernatorial margin history: Kemp d. Abrams by 1.4 points (2018), then by 7.5 points (2022); Deal's 2010 open-seat win ran wider still. No tight, predictable band the way the state's recent Senate races have shown - this reference class argues for caution about false precision, not a specific number.
Trump's approval in Georgia running underwater (43-45% approve / 51-53% disapprove per AJC's April and Wick's June 2026 polls) - a structural headwind on the GOP brand heading into his first midterm.
Republican-held governorships Democrats flipped in the 2018 midterm, the closest analog to 2026's setup (a Republican president's first midterm) - the out-party structural tailwind reference class.

Outgoing Gov. Brian Kemp's own approval and net favorability in Georgia - evidence voters can credit Republican governance even while souring on Trump nationally, the split-ticket risk case for Jackson.
The debate-dodge market swing: Bottoms moved from underdog to favorite on PredictIt and Kalshi between her June 23 debate challenge and mid-July, when Jackson had still not responded.

Jackson has self-funded $108M+ (including an $87M ad blitz largely still airing) against Bottoms's roughly $250K cash-on-hand as of her May 2026 filing - a spending mismatch not yet reflected in a Jackson lead.

markets.detail: A swept search turned up no active Manifold or Metaculus market specifically on the 2026 Georgia governor winner (unlike the 2026 GA Senate race, which has both). Not used as an anchor — noted as absent rather than invented.

triggers: Jackson agreeing to a debate (or a second, sharper refusal) - either resolves the single biggest live signal markets are currently pricing off.

A post-Labor-Day likely-voter poll (not the June Wick registered/likely mix) showing the race back inside 3 points, or alternatively Bottoms opening a lead past 8-10 points - either would move the consensus band materially.
Jackson's $87M ad blitz fully airing without narrowing the polling gap by early October - would harden the Bottoms lean; a visible narrowing would flip it.
A public reconciliation or active campaigning for Jackson by Burt Jones or Trump-aligned Georgia Republicans - signals the primary fracture is healing, favors Jackson.
A national macro or Trump-approval shock (further erosion below 40% approval in Georgia, or a rebound past 48%) - the single largest driver of the out-party tailwind either direction.
A surge in Kalshi or PredictIt volume with the price holding in the mid-50s - would upgrade market confidence from 'directional' to 'load-bearing' anchor.
Democratic primary turnout advantage failing to show up in fall registration/early-vote data - would undercut the Prophet's and Historian's structural read.
A credible independent/third-party candidate polling above 3-4% - mechanically raises the runoff branch under Georgia's 50%+1 rule.

method_note: Anchored on a three-market composite (Polymarket ~59%, Kalshi 55-58%, PredictIt 54%) that converged in the mid-50s for Bottoms after Jackson declined her June 23 debate challenge - a real, dated market-moving event, not an assumption. Because Georgia's own gubernatorial margin history is wide (1.4 to 7.5 points across the last two cycles) rather than tight, and because Jackson's $87M ad blitz is still largely unspent against Bottoms's roughly $250K cash-on-hand, the raw market composite is marked down slightly rather than taken at face value: consensus lands at 53-61% for Bottoms, not the high-50s the composite alone implies. No liquid Manifold or Metaculus market was found on this specific race and none was invented. Horizon: through November 3, 2026.
honesty_note: The modal call — a narrow-to-moderate Bottoms win at 53-61% — is a lean, not a settled outcome, and it rests on markets thinner than a typical federal race (Polymarket's total volume is under $60,000) plus a single scheduling event (the debate dodge) doing a lot of the work in the recent price movement. A near-even Wick poll from late June is real, unresolved counter-evidence. Treat this as the best current read, not a call that should survive unchanged through three more months of $100M+ in advertising.
